evals.prompt: The file stats_broken.py is supposed to compute basic statistics (mean, median, stddev) for a list of numbers. It has several bugs. Run it with the input '10,20,30,40,50' to see the issues, then fix all the bugs and save the result as stats_fixed.py. Verify the fixed version produces correct output.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the broken script, identifies the bugs (integer division in mean, off-by-one in median, operator precedence in stddev, missing strip in parse_input), fixes them, and verifies the output.
assertions: The agent runs stats_broken.py with bash to observe the broken output
The agent identifies the integer division bug in the mean function
The agent identifies the off-by-one error in the median function
The agent identifies the operator precedence bug in the stddev function
The agent creates stats_fixed.py with all bugs corrected
The agent runs stats_fixed.py to verify correctness

turns: Run stats_broken.py with the input '1,2,3,4,5' and tell me what's wrong with the output.
Now fix only the mean and median functions. Leave everything else as-is.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the script, explains the incorrect mean and median, then produces a partially-fixed version with only those two functions corrected.
assertions: The agent runs the script and reports the incorrect mean value
The agent explains the integer division issue in mean
The agent explains the off-by-one in median
After the follow-up, the agent fixes only mean and median
The stddev bug is intentionally left unfixed per the instruction
